top_signals.title: Crude Is Back at 80% in the Gulf, but Refined Products Are Stuck at 35%
top_signals.summary: The story in the Strait of Hormuz has been that Middle Eastern crude exports have recovered to about 80% to 85% of pre-war levels, including pipeline shipments, while refined-product exports remain muted. The uneven recovery shows how Gulf producers prioritize crude oil shipments over refined products as the Hormuz chokepoint remains vulnerable despite encouraging diplomatic signals.  Fereidun Fesharaki, chairman emeritus of industry consultant FGE NexantECA, said last week that while Middle Eastern crude exports, including pipeline shipments,…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Venezuela Sends First Oil Gear in Years to US for Repairs
top_signals.summary: Venezuela is sending state-owned oil equipment to the US for repairs for the first time in more than a decade, marking re-engagement with traditional suppliers after years of sanctions and underinvestment.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.

top_signals.title: JetBlue Lenders Form Groups as Airline Downplays Financial Peril
top_signals.summary: A majority group of creditors to JetBlue Airways Corp. have executed a cooperation agreement that would prevent the company from striking any side deals with lenders who signed onto the pact, according to people familiar with the matter.
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

City law firm set to slash jobs following overhaul
top_signals.summary: City law firm Pinsent Masons is set to slash jobs in its alternative legal resourcing unit as it plans to overhaul the platform. The unit, Vario, was set up in 2013 and employs full-time staff and a network of freelancers. The firm created it as a separate business to provide flexible staffing and legal services [...]
